summary: Charles Goodman works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan in 2002 under Allan Gibbard and is attested as an associate professor at Binghamton University in 2013.

Charles H. Long (1926–2020) was a religious studies scholar educated at Dunbar Junior College and the University of Chicago (BD, PhD). He held posts at Chicago, UNC Chapel Hill, Duke, Syracuse, and UC Santa Barbara.

Charles Hallisey is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Colgate, Harvard, UPenn, and the University of Chicago (PhD 1988). He has held faculty posts at Loyola University Chicago, Harvard University, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Charles Hamilton (1752–1792) was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He served in the military with the East India Company from 1776 and was an early member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1792).

Charles Harris (1859–1943) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned degrees from Indiana University Bloomington and the University of Leipzig (PhD 1884 under Ernst Windisch), later serving as professor of German at Oberlin College and Case Western Reserve University.

Charles Henry Allan Bennett (1872–1923) worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He founded the Buddhasasana Samagama and The Buddhist Review, and served as head of the Buddhist Society of Great Britain and Ireland in 1908.

Charles Henry Tawney (1837–1922) was an Indologist educated at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as professor and head at Presidency University, principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, registrar at the University of Calcutta, and librarian at the India Office.

Charles Hubert Biddulph (1898–1966) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at Philander Smith College and the Crystal Palace School of Engineering, he served in various engineering and managerial roles at the South Indian Railway Company (1924–1966).
Charles Hyart (1913–2004) was a linguist who studied under René Fohalle at the University of Liège, where he later taught Russian.

Charles James Lyall (1845–1920) was a linguist and Indologist educated at King's College School, King's College London, and Balliol College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1867–1898) and as professor of Arabic at Oxford (1913–1920).

Charles James Rodgers (1838–1898) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar educated at Borough Road College and Cambridge. He was principal of the Christian Vernacular Education Society Training College, Amritsar, and Honorary Numismatist to the Government of India.

Charles Johnston (1867–1931) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1884–1888). In 1908, he served as a special lecturer in political science at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Charles Jones Ogden (1880–1955) worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Columbia University under A. V. Williams Jackson and served there as an honorary lecturer in Indo-Iranian languages (1926–1931).
Charles Lecoutere (1865–1921) was a linguist who studied under Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin at KU Leuven, completing his PhD in 1892. He was appointed professor at KU Leuven in 1895.

Charles Li is a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and computational fields. He earned his PhD from the University of Cambridge (2018) and held positions at UBC, CNRS (2020–2023), and the University of Hamburg (2023).

Charles Louis Fabri (1899–1968) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Pécs and Leiden under Sylvain Lévi and Jean Philippe Vogel. He held positions at Leiden, Visva-Bharati, the Archaeological Survey of India, and Lahore Museum.

Charles Malamoud is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris. He held academic posts at the University of Lyon (~1961–1972) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1979–1998).
Charles Masson (1800–1853) was an Indology and history/archaeology researcher who served as an agent for the East India Company (~1822–1826) and the Government of India (~1834–1838).

Charles Matthew Whish (1794–1833) was an Indologist and historian who studied at East India Company College and the College of Fort St. George. He served with the East India Company and in the Madras Presidency from 1812.

Charles Michel (1853–1929) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Félix Nève at KU Leuven and Abel Bergaigne at the University of Paris. He served as professor at Ghent University and the University of Liège.
